negative_reviews.author: Ben McEwan
negative_reviews.text: Sold me tokyo sunrise cocktail costing 10 pounds but it’s 99 percent ice and less than 20ml of liquid   Got scammed by them selling a cocktail with tiny amount of liquid/alcohol and they refuse to make it right. Then they charge a service charge on top of the cocktail so I’m out over 11 pounds total for their cocktail that’s mostly ice.  I had to empty out the ice onto a plate to try get liquid since I was so dehydrated.

negative_reviews.author: Ruth Flynn
negative_reviews.text:
Although the ramen and food were lovely, the customer service was disappointing, especially from the manager.

I’ve visited several times with colleagues and friends, hoping each visit would be better, but unfortunately we have left disappointed every time. The staff were not accommodating to customers’ needs, and the overall service lacked warmth and professionalism.

What made the experience even more frustrating was that a service charge was already included in the bill, even though it is optional. This puts customers in an awkward position and makes the dining experience uncomfortable. A service charge should reflect good service, not be assumed.

The food is genuinely good, but the consistently poor customer service means I cannot recommend this place until it improves.

negative_reviews.author: Afterlife Addict
negative_reviews.text:
I gave Maki & Ramen a second chance, and I instantly regretted it.

The food wasn’t even the biggest issue. The customer service, especially from the manager, completely ruined the experience. Instead of listening to our concerns or trying to find a solution, the manager was defensive throughout the conversation. We weren’t expecting anything unreasonable, just some understanding and a willingness to resolve the situation.

To make matters worse, we were still charged a mandatory service charge, despite receiving service that was far below expectations. It’s disappointing to be expected to pay extra for an experience that left us feeling ignored.

What made this even more frustrating was that we had guests visiting from overseas, and this ended up ruining what should have been an enjoyable evening.

Unfortunately, after giving this restaurant another chance, I won’t be returning. If you’re looking for ramen in Glasgow, I’d recommend trying Ramen Dayo instead. The difference in customer service and overall experience is night and day.
